extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in autoformalization, theorem proving, and benchmark/metric design (AI/formal_methods community)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating end-to-end pipelines that read informal math problems, formalize them in Lean, and produce formal proofs; and designing/curating benchmarks (miniF2F and miniF2F-v2) to measure such systems. The focus is on pipeline accuracy, statement alignment, dataset correctness, and diagnosing failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-to-end pipeline credit condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The model has to read and comprehend the problems in natural language, formalize them in Lean language, then proceed with proving the problems, and it will get credit for each problem if the formal proof corresponds to the original informal statement presented to the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation gives credit only when the produced formal proof corresponds to the original informal statement; partial or mismatched formalizations that do not reflect the informal problem should not be credited. This defines the end-to-end success condition for the task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipeline accuracy as primary metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the proportion of problems the full pipeline (autoformalization + theorem prover) solves correctly; reported as accuracy (e.g., best observed ~36% for the pipeline in prior SoTA combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare end-to-end pipeline accuracy against component SoTA numbers (autoformalization and theorem proving individually) to reveal gaps: the paper notes much lower pipeline accuracy (≈36%) compared to individual component accuracies (97% and 69% reported in autoformalization and theorem proving literature). Use pipeline accuracy to quantify real-world effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment / consistency between formal and informal statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal and informal problem statements must correspond closely; discrepancies between them degrade measured performance (the authors trace a considerable portion of accuracy drop to such discrepancies, affecting more than half the problems in miniF2F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that the formalization preserves the intent and constraints of the informal statement; detect and correct simplifications, errors, or mismatches. When evaluating models, control for statement alignment to avoid penalizing models for benchmark annotation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset correctness and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-quality benchmark requires fully verified formal and informal statements and proofs (the authors corrected errors, discrepancies and simplifications and present miniF2F-v2 with fully verified formal and informal statements and proofs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks should be curated so that both the informal descriptions and their formal counterparts (and reference proofs) are checked and verified. Verified datasets reduce noise in evaluation and permit more meaningful comparisons across systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of corrected/cleaned benchmarks to measure true system capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating the pipeline on a corrected benchmark (miniF2F-v2) yields substantially higher accuracy (best accuracy 70%) compared to the original benchmark (40%), indicating that dataset quality materially affects measured performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting system performance, evaluate on cleaned/verified versions of benchmarks to avoid conflating model shortcomings with dataset annotation errors. Use before/after comparisons to quantify impact of dataset corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure-mode analysis and diagnostic evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing failure modes of the pipeline to trace errors back to their sources (e.g., autoformalization mistakes vs theorem prover limitations) is essential to understanding performance drops and misalignment between components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform systematic analyses to separate errors due to incorrect formalization from those due to proving failures. Use such diagnostics to guide improvements in models and benchmark design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark design principle: enable progress measurement and diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher quality benchmark can help the community better evaluate progress in the field of formal reasoning and also better diagnose the failure and success modes of autoformalization and theorem proving models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design benchmarks not only to measure final scores but to enable interpretable diagnosis (e.g., clear mapping between informal and formal statements, metadata about transformations, and annotations that help pinpoint where pipelines fail).
